title: Decimals to Thousandths
short: Read and write decimals in digits, words and expanded form.

blocks.html: You can read tenths and hundredths. Cut a hundredth into 10 equal parts and you get a thousandth, the third place after the decimal point.

After the decimal point the places are tenths, hundredths, thousandths. To read a decimal, read the whole number, say “and” for the point, read the digits after the point as one number, and finish with the name of the last place.

$0.347$ is $\frac{3}{10} + \frac{4}{100} + \frac{7}{1000}$. Rename the tenths and hundredths as thousandths: $\frac{300}{1000} + \frac{40}{1000} + \frac{7}{1000} = \frac{347}{1000}$. That is why the whole decimal part can be read as “three hundred forty-seven thousandths.”

blocks.title: Words to digits
blocks.q: Write “five and twelve thousandths” in digits.
steps: “Thousandths” means three places after the point, with the 12 ending in the thousandths place.
So the places are 0 tenths, 1 hundredth, 2 thousandths.

blocks.title: Expanded form
steps: There are no hundredths, so the hundredths place gets a 0.

blocks.html: Leaving out a placeholder zero, like writing “five and twelve thousandths” as $5.12$. That is five and twelve hundredths. Check: the last digit must land in the place the last word names.
